newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA CALLING IN FOREIGN EXPERTS IN AIDS REVIEW.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA CALLING IN FOREIGN EXPERTS IN AIDS REVIEW.

text.p: South Africa is roping in a team of international experts to help it review its progress in fighting AIDS, a health official said on Friday.

Rose Smart, director of the national health department's programme to combat AIDS and HIV, said research teams including officials from the World Health Organisation would review government policies and South Africa's response to the AIDS epidemic.
She told a briefing it would be the first review of AIDS prevention programmes in South Africa since the first AIDS case in the country was reported 15 years ago.
The review is intended to come up with recommendations to advance the fight against the disease in South Africa.
An estimated 2.5 million of the country's 38 million people are believed to be infected with HIV.
